newsitem.title: CHINA: China foreign minister to visit Russia.
newsitem.headline: China foreign minister to visit Russia.

text.p: China's Vice-Premier and Foreign Minister Qian Qichen will visit Russia later this month, a ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.
Qian will visit Russia from March 24-27 at the invitation of Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, the spokesman told a news briefing. He gave no further details.

Beijing and Moscow, once arch-rivals for leadership of the communist world, have been steadily building warmer and closer ties for the last decade, and relations have improved even more quickly since the collapse of the Soviet Union.
Chinese President Jiang Zemin is to visit Moscow in April to sign a pact to reduce troops along China's border with Russia and the central Asian states of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan.
China and Russia clashed along their border in the 1960s when the two nuclear powers were at odds, and there have long been border disputes between the five countries.
Basic agreement on the demarcation of the 4,300-km (2,671-mile) Sino-Russian border, the main boundary in the highly volatile region, was finally reached in 1991.
Beijing and Moscow have ruled out any revival of the close military and political alliance that existed in the 1950s.
